findings.reason: a node told to fix "section by section" dispatch will find no such instruction and may leave the ready-only filter in place, which is the actual obstacle §16 exists to remove.
findings.text: §16 says "The build skill still tells them to dispatch section by section on each beat", but the instruction it cites and removes, `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:141` "Fill the lane every beat. Read the ready-idle set: sections that are implementable, dependency-ready and gate-clear with no live run... Dispatch every one of your own, critical-path links first", already instructs dispatching every ready section in one beat, not one section at a time; the real remaining gap is that the selection is filtered to *dependency-ready* sections, so a section whose upstream is unlanded is excluded rather than queued

findings.reason: a done-when that a cosmetic rewording satisfies cannot show the new dispatch rule landed, and §16's whole purpose is that rule.
findings.text: §16's measure greps `skills/` and `AGENTS.md` for three literal phrases and requires their absence, but the behaviour the body wants is a change in the selection rule (dispatch every remaining section, parking unlanded ones `awaiting-upstream`); removing or rewording "Fill the lane every beat" satisfies the grep while leaving the dependency-ready filter — the exact mechanism that excludes not-yet-ready sections — untouched, so the measure can pass without the deliverable

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified live and resolving: `require_plan_reviewed` (reckon/crew/routing.py:2489), `admit_once` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2188), `section_waits_for` (:1099), `derive_wait_refs` (:1136), the flight key `plan_review_gate: enforce` (reckon/flight.py:78-79, ~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml:88), the five skill files, AGENTS.md, and the `crew view live` / `crew view drain` names (reckon/mcp_views.py:3785 CREW_VIEWS); the queue verbs `edit`/`reprioritise`/`drop` all exist on `reckon crew queue`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's grep arm measures the absence of three literal phrases rather than the dispatch rule the body wants in their place, so it can pass on a reworded phrase while the dependency-ready filter survives.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither section places a gate log or evidence file in a scratchpad or node-local temporary path; the measures are test arms and a grep run at the landing beat, recorded in the run record.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §11's `plan-review-owed` and `held` are data values in the request-phase vocabulary, and neither section introduces a symbol, filename or comment carrying a plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16's stated root cause ("the build skill still tells them to dispatch section by section on each beat") is contradicted by the instruction its own done-when quotes and removes (see FINDING reasoning s16). §11's three mechanisms were checked and hold: the gate does run again on a queued launch through `dispatch_plan` (`require_plan_reviewed` called at reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:854 with `enforce=flight.plan_review_gate_enforces(config)`), the host layer does set `plan_review_gate: enforce`, and `derive_wait_refs` is exactly the union §11 now describes (section refs + plan `depends_on` + `node.after` run refs), while `section_waits_for` reads only the stored `waits`. `crew queue edit` (checked: `--brief/--done-when/--write-path/--time-budget/--backend/--model`) cannot set waits, so §11's per-pass rewrite does not clobber a coordinator's explicit wait edit.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 owns one deliverable (a plan edit neither strands a queued request nor leaves its waits stale) and §16 owns one (the skill instructions load a plan's full width and link sections); each done-when closes that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s11 depends on s10 (the `held` phase it moves a refused request into) and s16 depends on s3 (the per-session cap lift it follows); every `depends-on` ref in `plan-section-depends-on` resolves to a node that exists and is declared, and no cited relationship points at the wrong node.
